content: 1. A study published in Antiviral Therapy in 2008 (Volume 13, Issue 3, Pages 429–437) examined the treatment of chronic hepatitis C with abacavir. 2. Research by Laufer N, Laguno M, Perez I, Cifuentes C, Murillas J, Vidal F, et al., published in Antiviral Therapy in 2008 (Volume 13, Issue 7, Pages 953–957), concluded that abacavir does not affect the virological response rate in HIV-HCV co-infected patients treated with pegylated interferon and weight-adjusted ribavirin. 3. El-Raziky MS, El-Hawary M, Esmat G, Abouzied AM, El-Koofy N, Mohsen N, et al., in a study published in World Journal of Gastroenterology in 2007 (Volume 13, Issue 12, Pages 1828–1832), investigated the prevalence and risk factors of asymptomatic hepatitis C virus infection in Egyptian children. 4. Locasciulli A, Gornati G, Tagger A, Ribeiro ML, Cavalletto D, Cavalletto L, et al., in a 1991 study published in Blood (Volume 78, Issue 6, Pages 1619–1622), explored hepatitis C virus infection and chronic liver disease in children with leukemia in long-term remission. 5. Rossetti F, Cesaro S, Pizzocchero P, Cadrobbi P, Guido M, Zanesco L, in a study published in Journal of Pediatrics in 1992 (Volume 121, Issue 1, Pages 39–43), examined chronic hepatitis B surface antigen-negative hepatitis following malignancy treatment. 6. Jonas MM, Zilleruelo GE, LaRue SI, Abitbol C, Strauss J, Lu Y, in a study published in Pediatrics in 1992 (Volume 89, Issue 4, Part 2, Pages 707–709), investigated hepatitis C infection in a pediatric dialysis population. 7. Greco M, Cristiano K, Leozappa G, Rapicetta M, Rizzoni G, in a study published in Pediatric Nephrology in 1993 (Volume 7, Issue 4, Pages 424–427), examined hepatitis C infection in children and adolescents undergoing hemodialysis and after renal transplantation. 8. Nelson SP and Jonas MM, in a study published in Journal of Pediatric Surgery in 1996 (Volume 31, Issue 5, Pages 644–648), investigated hepatitis C infection in children who underwent extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 9. Ni YH, Chang MH, Lue HC, Hsu HY, Wang MJ, Chen PJ, et al., in a study published in Journal of Pediatrics in 1994 (Volume 124, Issue 5, Part 1, Pages 709–713), explored post-transfusion hepatitis C virus infection in children. 10. Thomas DL, Astemborski J, Rai RM, Anania FA, Schaeffer M, Galai N, et al., in a study published in JAMA in 2000 (Volume 284, Issue 4, Pages 450–456), examined the natural history of hepatitis C virus infection, focusing on host, viral, and environmental factors. 11. Potthoff A, Wedemeyer H, Boecher WO, Berg T, Zeuzem S, Arnold J, et al., in the HEP-NET B/C co-infection trial published in Journal of Hepatology in 2008 (Volume 49, Issue 5, Pages 688–694), conducted a prospective multicenter study to evaluate the efficacy of pegylated interferon-alpha 2b and ribavirin in patients with HBV/HCV co-infection. 12. Pérez-Elías MJ, García-San Miguel L, González García J, Montes Ramírez ML, Muriel A, Machín-Lázaro JM, et al., in a study published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2009 (Volume 48, Issue 8, Pages e82–e85), investigated tuberculosis as a complication during hepatitis C treatment in HIV-infected patients. 13. Gilks CF, Crowley S, Ekpini R, Gove S, Perriens J, Souteyrand Y, et al., in a study published in The Lancet in 2006 (Volume 368, Issue 9534, Pages 505–510), discussed the World Health Organization's public health approach to antiretroviral treatment for HIV in resource-limited settings.
